problem: The opening definition 'Abnormal combustion is any burning that does not follow the spark-plug flame front' is too broad and can mislead. In ordinary knock, most of the charge still burns normally from the spark flame front; only the end gas burns abnormally. A student may conclude that in knock nothing burns from the plug.
fix: Say it as: 'Abnormal combustion is burning that departs from the normal spark-ignited flame sweep — either the end gas self-ignites, or a hot spot ignites the charge on its own.'

problem: The chapter presents knock only as a petrol-engine event ('You meet it in petrol engines ...'). Compression-ignition engines also knock, from a long ignition delay and a sudden pressure rise, and students often lose marks by writing 'knock occurs only in SI engines'.
fix: Add one sentence: 'CI engines also knock — there it comes from a long ignition delay and a sudden pressure rise, called diesel knock; the SI end-gas picture above does not apply to it.'
